# The exact flux joining surface-log and tilted-volume boundary defects

This is a limit identity for the ACTUAL logarithmic contact rows. It joins the previously retained tilted-volume defect to an unscaled surface-logarithm defect. It neither identifies the ordinary cap-stress coupling with the volume coupling nor proves that either defect vanishes.

Dependencies are `candidate 8ba63f3af7e6943f`, the trace proof in `candidate 79036a0d1b9e182a`, and normal-bundle surface-area convergence as proved in `candidate 714f69e684c396b1`. The first dependency was independently audited in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. Exact hypotheses and notation

Let P be finite, d>=1, and let positive convex fibers K_z^j tend to K_z in Hausdorff distance. They have a common outer radius R, uniform inballs, and positive lower volumes. Denote mixed volume by dm_j, total mass by M_j, and the limits by dm,M. Use the subsequence and finite source labels supplied by the contact-row limit theorem. Thus

    max L_j<=L_*,  mean_(m_j) log L_j=0,
    L_ij=L_j(Y_ij)>=l_*>0,
    B(y_ij,r_s) subset K_(p_i)^j,
    E_(rho_ij) w=Y_ij,  E_(rho_ij) L_j=L_ij,
    sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij) rho_ij=dm_j/(M_j L_j),
    sigma_ij>0,  sum_i sigma_ij=1.                    (1)

The finite-plane representatives can be chosen as

    L_j=min_i A_ij -> L=min_i A_i                    (2)

uniformly on a common ambient compact box, with bounded affine coefficients. On each sampled limiting fiber, L is nonnegative, positive in the interior, and log-normalized. Its reciprocal is integrable. Each surviving source has L_i>0 and a unique continuous gradient c_i, the limit of c_ij. The affine plane A_i touches that source and equals L on its entire limiting contact row. Labels whose sigma_i is zero make no contribution below.

Retain the full inverse-volume limit, including its labeled defects:

    nu_j=dm_j/(M_j L_j) -> dm/(M L)+zeta,
    zeta_i=(sigma_i/L_i) rho_i restricted_to {L=0},
    zeta=sum_i zeta_i.                               (3)

All measure convergence here and below is weak convergence on a fixed compact ambient space. Base coordinates remain discrete. No uniform integrability of 1/L_j is assumed.

Let eta_j be the surface-area measure of the sampled fibers with their actual outward unit continuous normals recorded:

    integral F d eta_j
      =sum_z integral_(boundary K_z^j) F(n_z^j(X),z,X) dS.

The a.e. unique normal is sufficient to define this measure. The convex-body normal-bundle convergence theorem gives eta_j -> eta. It retains normals at nonsmooth limiting points through the normal-bundle coordinate. In d=1 these are the two endpoint counting measures in each fiber.

## 2. A positive surface defect exists and is supported over {L=0}

Define the nonnegative boundary measures

    b_j=(-log L_j)_+ eta_j.

They have uniformly bounded mass. Indeed the exact contact-gradient identity and the source inballs give

    integral |grad_X log L_j| dm_j <= M_j/r_s,
    integral |log L_j| dm_j <=2 M_j log L_*.

Choose fixed limiting inball centers g_z, with a reduced radius r_b>0 so that they are also common inball centers for all sufficiently large j. Gauss--Green applied fiberwise to (X-g_z)|log L_j| gives

    r_b integral |log L_j| d eta_j
      <=d integral |log L_j| dm_j
          +2R integral |grad_X log L_j| dm_j.         (4)

Enlarge R if necessary so that |X-g_z|<=2R. Consequently a subsequence has b_j -> b_total.

The limiting ordinary trace (-log L)_+ is integrable on the boundary. Here is an argument retaining possible zeros. The finite-plane function L is Lipschitz on each fiber and has bounded gradient. Since integral 1/L is finite, log(L+delta) tends to log L in W^(1,1)(K_z) as delta decreases to zero: its gradients are dominated by C/L and its logarithms are dominated by an integrable negative logarithm plus a constant. Apply the radial trace estimate (4) to differences log(L+delta)-log(L+delta'). The boundary traces are Cauchy in L1. On the boundary set where L>0 they converge pointwise to log L.

The remaining set {L=0} has zero surface area. Each zero set of a nonnegative affine plane is an exposed face. If such a face had dimension d-1, an inner cone from it to an interior ball would give a divergent integral of 1/L, since L<=A and the transversal integral contains integral_0^a ds/s. Thus every zero face has dimension at most d-2. There are only finitely many planes. For d=1 no zero is possible. This identifies the L1 trace with log L a.e. and also proves Gauss--Green for log L by passage from log(L+delta).

Put b_0=(-log L)_+ eta. Then

    b_total=b_0+b,  b>=0,
    support(b) subset {(n,z,X):X in K_z, L(z,X)=0}.
                                                            (5)

To check positivity, use the continuous bounded truncation

    f_T(s)=min{(-log s)_+,T} for s>0,
           T for s<=0.

Uniform convergence (2) and eta_j -> eta imply f_T(L_j)eta_j -> f_T(L)eta. Since b_j dominates this measure, b_total dominates f_T(L)eta; let T increase to infinity. On any compact subset where L>0 the untruncated weights converge uniformly, proving equality there and the support assertion in (5).

The positive logarithmic part has no defect:

    (log L_j)_+ eta_j -> (log L)_+ eta,               (6)

because s -> log(max{1,s}) is continuous and uniformly bounded on the common parameter range. Hence the signed boundary logarithms converge to log L eta-b.

## 3. Exact vector Gauss--Green identity

The labeled volume rows give an identity of vector measures before taking limits:

    grad_X log L_j dm_j
       =M_j sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij)c_ij rho_ij.         (7)

At volume-a.e. point of row i, grad_X L_j=c_ij. The finite-plane creases with different continuous gradients are volume-null; base-only ties have the same continuous gradient. Taking limits in the finite sum (7), then using the labeled limit decomposition, gives

    grad_X log L_j dm_j
       -> grad_X log L dm + M sum_i c_i zeta_i.      (8)

This is an exact weak identity, not a lower-semicontinuity inequality. Terms with sigma_i=0 vanish because L_ij has a positive lower bound and c_ij is uniformly bounded.

For any scalar test phi(z,X) that is C1 in X on a common neighborhood (with independent choices on the finite bases), fiberwise Gauss--Green gives

    integral phi log L_j n d eta_j
      =integral [log L_j grad_X phi
                          +phi grad_X log L_j] dm_j. (9)

The ordinary bulk log term converges by the uniform log integrability proved in the contact-row limit theorem. Equations (5)--(8) pass every other term. Subtracting the limiting-body Gauss--Green identity proves

    - integral phi(z,X) n db(n,z,X)
          =M sum_i c_i integral phi(z,X) d zeta_i.   (10)

Equivalently, as vector Radon measures on the physical sampled set,

    - pi_*(n b)=M sum_i c_i zeta_i.                  (11)

Here pi forgets only the normal coordinate. Formula (10) extends to continuous physical scalar tests by density. For any C1 continuous-vector test V_z(X), it reads

    - integral V_z(X).n db
          =M sum_i integral c_i.V_z(X) d zeta_i.     (12)

One may isolate a single base throughout. There is no unproved normal-dependent test on the right: the tilted defect has no independently specified normal coordinate.

No internal-interface term occurs in (9): a continuous finite-PL L_j has a first weak gradient with no crease measure, and log L_j is continuous. In contrast, applying Gauss--Green separately after multiplying by indicators of its gradient cells introduces internal cell-interface terms. Thus (10) retains volume labels on its right but does NOT assert an unaudited surface splitting b_i satisfying -n b_i=M c_i zeta_i individually.

## 4. A positive radial identity and exact equivalence of defect vanishing

Use V_z(X)=X-g_z in (12), with the fixed inball centers from Section 2. Every limiting normal in the support of b is a genuine support normal of K_z; hence

    r_b<=n.(X-g_z)<=2R.

On zeta_i, the contact identity gives A_i(z,X)=L(z,X)=0. Since A_i is affine with continuous gradient c_i,

    c_i.(X-g_z)=-A_i(z,g_z).

Therefore the vector flux has the following positive scalar consequence:

    integral n.(X-g_z) db
       =M sum_i integral A_i(z,g_z) d zeta_i.        (13)

Let

    a_0=min_z L(z,g_z)>0,
    A_0=max_(surviving i,z) A_i(z,g_z)<infinity.

Every touching plane majorizes L, so a_0<=A_i(z,g_z)<=A_0. It follows that

    [M a_0/(2R)] zeta(S) <= b(total)
                         <=[M A_0/r_b] zeta(S).      (14)

The same statement holds per fiber with its own constants. In particular

    b=0 if and only if zeta=0.                       (15)

Thus cancellation of the vector gradients in (10) cannot hide a nonzero total defect: the actual support geometry supplies the positive radial test. This is a relation between two possible defects, not an argument eliminating them at a body minimum.

## 5. Exact nonzero calibration on the truncated triangles

Use the actual one-source sequence from `candidate 1b1d5e313c1943d1`:

    a=1/m, eta=2^(-m), b=a-eta,
    K_m={x,y>=0:a<=x+y<=1},
    L_m=c_m(x+y-b),  c_m->c=exp(1/2).

The new cut facet has length sqrt(2)/m, normal n_0=-(1,1)/sqrt(2), and constant parameter value c_m 2^(-m). Its negative-log boundary mass is eventually

    [sqrt(2)/m][m log 2-log c_m] -> sqrt(2) log 2.

It collapses to the origin. The coordinate sides produce no extra defect: their log integral has the primitive (s log s-s), and the lower-end term eta log eta tends to zero. Away from the origin their weights converge uniformly. The top facet has no negative-log contribution for all sufficiently large m. Consequently

    b=sqrt(2) log 2 delta_(n_0,(0,0)).                (16)

The tilted-volume theorem gives

    zeta=2 exp(-1/2) log 2 delta_(0,0),
    M=1/2,  c_1=c(1,1).

Then both sides of (10), with phi=1, equal (log 2,log 2). Taking g=(1/3,1/3), both sides of (13) equal (2/3)log 2. This verifies the orientation, the factor M, and the retained source-gradient factor by an actual nonzero example.

This sequence has uniformly interior contact sources but they are not deepest. It therefore calibrates (10)--(15) without answering whether additional limiting deepestness and full physical stationarity rule out the linked defects.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_surface_log_tilted_defect_flux_slab_recovery.py` independently checks exact polynomial-test Gauss--Green identities on the actual truncated triangles, the contact normalization identities, and the limiting vector/radial constants. The analytic weak convergence and normal-bundle statement are proved above, not inferred from those finite checks.
